title: The inclusive-captions pilot: high-level design
subtitle: Two SDXL LoRAs on the same 491 COCO photos, differing in one cell of a caption table, read on 128 shared seeds. Drawn 2026-11-04 from the plan and the code.
lede: Follow the spine left to right. Everything up to the caption rule is shared, and the two training lanes are the same part run twice on the same photographs. The only thing that differs is the caption rule each lane is handed, which is written on the two arrows into them. The lanes meet again at one scoring pass, which is what makes the two compose rates comparable.
version_line: Version 2, 2026-11-04: 12 boxes, 15 arrows, 9 pictures on 8 boxes. Read from the pilot plan, the walk map and the code.

details.heading: Where each box comes from
lines: COCO train2017: scripts/census/inclusive_captions_pool.py:69-71 reads instances_train2017.json and captions_train2017.json under /datasets/mmolefe/coco2017, with the images found at :81.
Pool builder: scripts/census/inclusive_captions_pool.py. The wanted counts are WANT at :105; the caption per photo is the shortest of each photo's five, at read_captions(), :128.

Photo audit, by eye: scripts/census/audit_both_animal_photos.py, 16 tiles a page at 448 pixels, nine pages for the 131. Its verdicts are committed at artifacts/results/the-inclusive-captions-photo-pool/audit-verdicts.json. The plan's instruction 8 owns the judging.
Photo manifest: /datasets/mmolefe/poe_repair_min/outputs/inclusive_captions_pool/manifest.json, written at inclusive_captions_pool.py:291. The four set sizes are the audited ones.

Caption rule, per draw: poe_repair/experiments/inclusive_captions/captions.py. The four caption strings are at :54-57, the 10% blank rate at :65, and the per-run shares on the both-animal photos at BOTH_SHARES, :69.

Run A and Run B: one part, poe_repair/experiments/inclusive_captions/trainer.py, run twice. It builds on poe_repair/_sdxl/runtime.py (load_sdxl_models, encode_prompt_sdxl, load_ddim_scheduler, decode_latents), puts the low-rank weights on with peft at build_lora(), trainer.py:107, and keeps the checkpoint steps at :67. It trains 46,448,640 weights at rank 32 on the four attention projections, and its 20-step smoke run finished green on mscluster111 in 225 seconds, writing step_00000 before any training (the plan's task 3.2).
LoRA adapters: trainer.py:60 and :188-189 write step_<n>/ under /datasets/mmolefe/poe_repair_min/outputs/inclusive_captions/<run>/, loadable with PeftModel.from_pretrained.

Weights & Biases: trainer.py:138-139 and :179-181, project prime_lab/poe-repair-inclusive-captions. The project was chosen new rather than as a group inside the animals-compose sweeps, per the walk map's decision table.

Watching sheet, written but not run: poe_repair/experiments/inclusive_captions/sheets.py exists, 221 lines, eight fixed seeds (0 to 7) down the rows and four columns across at 512 square and 25 steps, nine UNet forwards a step batched into one. The plan's tasks 4.1 and 4.2 are both open: it has not been run against a checkpoint, so it stays dashed.

Scoring pass, planned: the plan's tasks 6.1 and 6.2. The instrument already exists, GroundingDINO for the count and scripts/census/crop_classifier_cat_vs_dog.py for the names; the render-and-score pass over 128 product seeds per run does not.
Compose-rate figure, planned: the plan's task 6.3, filed under artifacts/results/do-inclusive-captions-help-poe-compose/ with its sidecar.

details.heading: How to read the lines
lines: A solid arrow is a read or a write that the step waits on; a dashed arrow is logging, which the step does not wait on.
The three dashed boxes are the parts that are not finished: the watching sheet (written, never run), the scoring pass and the figure.

The two arrows out of the caption rule carry the entire difference between the runs. Everything else about the two lanes, including the words on the boxes, is identical on purpose: the photos, the trainer, the blank-caption rate, the step count, the checkpoint steps and the seeds.

The one dashed arrow pointing left is the audit feeding back: the 40 rejected tile numbers are held as EXCLUDED_BOTH in the pool script, so the pool is re-run and the both-animal set drops from 131 to 91.
The caption rule is drawn as a service rather than a library because it is consulted on every draw, not once per run: run B resamples each both-animal photo's caption every time the photo comes up.
The dog-present share of run B's cat-captioned draws is 0.169, measured off 200,000 draws against the real manifest (the plan's task 2.3). Run A's is 0, which is what the comparison rests on.

A badge in a box's corner opens a picture: in for what goes into the box, out for what comes out, e.g. for one worked example of it. Any picture that is not this pilot's own output carries a label across the top saying where it came from, and the Weights & Biases panel is a drawing of the interface rather than a screenshot, because the project holds no runs yet.

details.heading: What is not drawn
lines: The compute. The two runs are started with nohup outside Slurm on a pinned free biggpu device reached over SSH, because biggpu allows one job per user, and they are harvested with pgrep rather than squeue. That is a fact about where the trainer boxes run, not a part of its own, so it stays in words.

The SDXL base model as a box. poe_repair/_sdxl/runtime.py supplies both text encoders, the VAE in fp32 and the UNet in fp16 inside the trainer's own process. It is a library in that box, not a separate running part, so it is named on the box instead. The fp16 upcast rule lives with it: a trainer that re-casts the VAE produces latents that do not match the sampling path.

The two runs the caption sampler also knows. captions.py:86 defines four runs, A, B, C and no-both. Only A and B are trained here: C was dropped and no-both is not in this plan, so neither gets a box.

The 48-tile contact sheets the pool script writes alongside the audit pages. They were too small to name a species off, which is why the audit render exists, so drawing both would show a path nobody uses.
The criterion. The review file holds the three outcomes and the band's formula, and the verdict is ticked by hand against the figure. It is a document and a judgment, not a running part.
The base-SDXL anchor named in the plan's task 6.3 figure. It is a third bar on the figure rather than a training run, so it has no lane.
Nothing is marked assumed. Every box and arrow here is named by the plan, the walk map or the code, with the file and line above.
The nine audit pages beyond the first. Page 1 is on the box; the other eight are the same thing for tiles 16 to 130 and would say nothing new.

opening.title: One difference, and everything else held still
paragraphs: Two SDXL LoRAs train on the same 491 COCO photographs. The only thing that differs is how the 91 both-animal photos are captioned, and that difference is written on the two arrows out of the caption rule in the middle.

Click any box to read what it is, where it comes from, and the pictures of what goes into it and what comes out. Eight of the twelve boxes carry one. Three boxes are drawn dashed: those parts are not finished yet.

how_to_read: A solid arrow is a read or a write the step waits on. A dashed arrow is logging, which it does not. A dashed box is a part that is not finished yet.
sources_note: Every box here is named by the pilot plan, the walk map or the code, with its file and line below. Nothing is drawn that one of those does not name.
